key_insight: VASPO combines a critic-based PPO value estimate with privileged self-teacher signals, using each where it is strongest to improve math-reasoning training.
engineering_relevance: For reasoning-model training, it offers a practical way to blend dense supervision and return-aware optimization, improving accuracy without relying only on GRPO-style signal scaling.
method: Compute PPO token-level advantages from a critic that predicts continuation returns at student-generated prefixes.
Use a self-teacher with privileged information to modulate selected positive advantages through bounded probability ratios.
Exploit complementary dynamics: critic is stronger near the end of responses, while self-teacher is strongest early and rebounds at the end.
evidence_signal: Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, VASPO improved mean accuracy over PPO by 2.59 points on Qwen3-4B and 1.81 points on OLMo3-7B, and achieved the best mean accuracy on Knights and Knaves.
watch_item: Because the method depends on careful coordination between critic estimates and self-teacher weighting, instability or miscalibration in either component could reduce the benefit.
paper_title: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation
